html:
The Chepenafa were a band of the Kalapuya people of Oregon's Willamette Valley, living along the Marys River near today's Corvallis.

Like other Kalapuya they lived by gathering camas bulbs and acorns, hunting deer, and burning the valley grasslands to keep them open. Disease in the 1830s killed most of the valley's people before settlers arrived along the Oregon Trail. In 1855 the Kalapuya signed a treaty giving up the valley and were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation. Their descendants belong to the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde.
sum: The Chepenafa were a band of the Kalapuya people of Oregon's Willamette Valley, living along the Marys River near today's Corvallis.
